Predict the retention of Millar's selectivity model

Source: R/predict.select_Millar.R
predict.select_Millar.Rd

Relative retention of a fitted selectivity model (select_Millar) for any lengths and mesh sizes.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'select_Millar'
predict(
  object,
  lengths = object$midLengths,
  meshSizes = object$meshSizes,
  rel.power = NULL,
  standardise = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a list of the class "select_Millar" with the results of select_Millar.

lengths

lengths for which the retention is predicted (default: the length classes of the fitted data).

meshSizes

mesh sizes for which the retention is predicted (default: the mesh sizes of the fitted data). The parameters of the model refer to the first (smallest) mesh size of the fitted data, which stays the reference mesh size for new mesh sizes.

rel.power

optional; relative fishing power of the mesh sizes (one value per mesh size). By default (NULL), the relative power of the fit is used if meshSizes are the fitted mesh sizes, otherwise 1.

standardise

logical; should the retention be divided by its maximum (Default: FALSE)?

...

unused.

Value

A matrix with the relative retention with one row per length and one column per mesh size.

Details

The retention curves have a maximum of 1 (except bi-modal curves and "tt.logistic"), multiplied with the relative power of the mesh size. For "tt.logistic", the retention of the control gear (mesh size equal to the reference mesh size) is 1 - p and of the experimental gear p times the logistic curve.

See also

select_Millar, select_Millar_curve

Examples

data(gillnet)
output <- select_Millar(gillnet, x0 = NULL, rtype = "lognorm", plot = FALSE)

## retention at the fitted mesh sizes
predict(output, lengths = seq(40, 90, 10))
#>            13.5           14         14.8         15.4         15.9
#> 40 4.137726e-04 6.244458e-05 2.335651e-06 1.660280e-07 1.658797e-08
#> 50 5.060169e-01 2.691024e-01 6.897279e-02 1.941783e-02 5.866897e-03
#> 60 5.435442e-01 8.089745e-01 9.991528e-01 8.660670e-01 6.463011e-01
#> 70 1.031329e-02 3.664257e-02 1.710401e-01 3.836639e-01 6.149459e-01
#> 80 1.687224e-05 1.273807e-04 1.881027e-03 9.614958e-03 2.988319e-02
#> 90 5.914385e-09 8.681135e-08 3.540442e-06 3.742166e-05 2.085826e-04
#>            16.6         17.8           19
#> 40 5.779795e-10 1.363332e-12 2.409029e-15
#> 50 9.090006e-04 2.404794e-05 4.070291e-07
#> 60 3.389027e-01 6.461861e-02 6.929337e-03
#> 70 9.039608e-01 9.155153e-01 4.676279e-01
#> 80 1.072831e-01 4.616077e-01 9.114487e-01
#> 90 1.646035e-03 2.536969e-02 1.650984e-01

## retention of a new mesh size
predict(output, lengths = seq(40, 90, 10), meshSizes = 16)
#>              16
#> 40 1.036140e-08
#> 50 4.553416e-03
#> 60 5.989843e-01
#> 70 6.621611e-01
#> 80 3.664257e-02
#> 90 2.868230e-04
